searchText: I know, I thought some will see the humor in Geth not even being in M0 😂 As you can see, we’ve already achieved this at Lighthouse. Don’t ask me how, just *believe* 🔮 hello, I have a non technical question about the merge, as far as I know, the stacked ETH on the beacon chain won't be available at the merge, will it be unlocked soon after that ? ( At the begining of the beacon chain I used a central exchange to stack ETH because my understanding of a node was low, now I want them back to do it at home to be more decentralised) iirc there will be a cleanup fork sometime soon after the merge where **staked** ether withdrawls will be enabled If it is staked on an exchange you will be able to unstake them on that exchange. Wish life was that easy 😅 Merge is going to make a lot of people broke. Lots of people (especially in third world countries) have mining as their primary source of income And also, really sad that merge is going to destroy this amazing and extremely fun hobby There's always Bitcoin if you want PoW Bitcoin is ASIC mined And ASIC manufacturers mostly work only with large corporations It’s a miracle to get a new, single ASIC mining unit for a regular person. Especially for those people from third world countries. I wasn't aware third world countries had better access to high-end graphics cards You don’t need a high end one A lot of low end GPUs do a really good job, and also a lot of people from third world countries have GPUs already. Is that possible to generate a own mining software which can work on the web 3 lands ? They can switch to staking instead of mining. If they haven’t enough Eth for a validator, there is still RocketPool or Lido There is no GPU-to-ETH converter And staking is no way near as profitable as mining Staking is more of a long term investment with a slim but stable APR Also staking is a lot more boring compared to mining With mining, you have to build your own rig, properly install drivers and configure GPUs for mining. Overclock them, make them mining more, optimize, optimize and optimize again! 😄 PC guys can definitely understand this, not sure about others though And there are a lot of YouTubers and huge community dedicated to this It's so sad that the Merge will ruin all this 😦 ? In conclusion, I'd say that mining is definitely more expensive, and it is definitely uses more power compared to PoS. But at the cost of this, it creates a wonderful part of the Ethereum community, fun hobby for crypto enthusiasts, a way to make money for people from the entire world, and brings a lot more interested people into the ecosystem in general. Also yes, correction: **GPU** mining ASIC mining is entirely different There is a fair bit of this around optimizing a node for running a validator. Tradeoffs of storage speed and capacity, vs RAM size for the geth cache, the different approaches for taking care of the networking side of things. .. just the work getting a full validator to work reliably on a raspberry pi involves overclocking the pi4 a bit. .. similar kinds of activities, just in a different dimension. Yeah, you are right. I've been in staking world too, and I remember the times of Beacon chain testnets - can't argue that they were fun. But they aren't as fun as mining, and staking doesn't make as much. As staking is not so profitable, it doesn't attract audience of users as wide as mining does. Just compare https://subredditstats.com/r/ethstaker and https://subredditstats.com/r/gpumining with https://subredditstats.com/r/ethstaker Also, looking at the top posts of both communities, it is clear that mining audience is more engaged compared to staking communities. I think that Ethereum Dev Team underestimates the weight of the mining community, and what they contribute to the ecosystem. Hey <@354681205842771973> can you please check my messages I did That profitability doesn't exist in a vacuum though. What would eth be worth if the merge wasn't on the horizon and there wasnt ~10% of the supply locked away into the beacon chain? Exactly Beacon chain attracts a lot of institutional investors to the ecosystem And mining attracts mostly the rest investors I think that the coexistence of Beacon chain and PoW during the same time period was the key in Ethereum's success Institutional investors (stakers) provided locked liquidity, which reduced the speculative pressure from the market as they now have a place to make their ETHs make more. Miners, on the other hand, attracted a lot of regular users and community members to the ecosystem and contributed to the wide adoption of Ethereum. more and more legislators are looking into the energy consumption of PoW, especially with the current events. It is not a bad idea to get things on track sooner than later Just give me a couple minutes I’ll send calculations here *Ethereum consumes 2.1 GW in total. That's 0.0000000863% of the total world's consumption. 0.2 W per person on our planet.* That's the calculation I've made a couple months ago. Unfortunately I couldn't find the source python script I used to calculate this. you don't have to convince me 😉 Hah ok Not that I would not think that 20TWh/anno should be saved if possible I think that 0.0000000863% of world’s consumption worth what mining provides to the Ethereum’s ecosystem. i will mine thc after merge and buy solar panels and sha256 asics from income thc? yep like chia 🙂 but more profitiable seeds and lamps I heard nothing about THC. What’s their daily network rewards? 10€ from one gram Pretty sure that no way near $45M daily Ethereum allocates for their mining ecosystem 3Kg montly You didn’t seem to get me. What’s the daily emission of your coin? Ah So 3k*10 EUR? Monthly? yep this is pretty far off topic. Definitely. What’s even more off topic is joking about weed…
